mike: Taking tonight oncall (slot 18:00-06:00 PT). I'm swapping with alice — she needs the morning. Quick FYI/watchlist before handoff.

mike: Known flaky signals to watch (non-incident): rt-inference latency spikes on 1s-10s timescales, and occasional KV cache evictions that cause brief error bursts for dedicated pools. Both have been noisy but not full outages. :eyes:

alice: Thanks — noted. History: rt-latency spikes usually correlate with >95th p50 request sizes (long contexts) or when batcher saturates. Last night Tara's rollback reduced spikes but not eliminated them.

tara: FYI I rolled back a model tweak at 03:20 UTC yesterday which helped the throughput, but we still saw bursts around 02:00-03:30 PT. I left a canary config change in the repo (see link) and plan a longer tuning next week.

mike: Primary mitigations if you see noisy alerts: 1) confirm it's a spike not a deploy (check /deploys or deploy-bot), 2) if spike < 10m and error rate < 1%, treat as noisy and silence per step below, 3) if persistent > 10m or error rate > 1% escalate to oncall-sre.

mike: Quick commands I use:
```
# view recent deploys
curl -s https://deploys.internal/api/recent | jq '.[] | {service,ref,time}' | head -n 20

# temporarily silence rt-latency alert for 15m
kubectl -n monitoring apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: monitoring/v1
kind: Silence
metadata:
  name: rt-latency-temp-silence
spec:
  duration: 15m
  matchers:
  - name: alertname
    value: "HighRTLatency"
EOF
```

alice: Good commands. Addendum: when silencing, post the silence ID back into the thread and include ETA. Also annotate any manual actions in the incident log (even if not promoted) so we can correlate.

ops-bot: [ALERT SUMMARY] 8 events in last 2h: 5 rt-latency spikes (avg duration 4.2m), 3 kv-eviction bursts. No error budget burn.

mike: Typical triage checklist (short):
- check deploy-bot for recent deploys (if yes, correlate)
- check model-serving logs for OOMs / GC pauses
- check batcher queue length (grafana: serving/batcher/queue_len)
- if KV eviction: check memory pressure on gpu-nodes and cache hitrate (metrics: cache/hit_ratio)

tara: For KV eviction, the short-term mitigation is to bump the eviction threshold on the affected pool (only for critical customers) — see playbook. Long-term: more aggressive prefix caching.

mike: Risk note: if you silence HighRTLatency too aggressively, we may miss an actual regression. Prefer short silences (10-20m) and check for recurrence.

alice: I'll take morning coverage from 06:00 — mike, I'll assume you keep the night until 06:00. If anything persistent pops, page: @oncall-sre and DM me.

mike: Confirmed. If I mute noisy alerts I'll post: "Silenced HighRTLatency (15m) due to noisy bursts; watching; will unmute or extend if pattern persists. --mike"

mike: Leaving a small watchlist for the handoff:
- rt-latency: look for >3 spikes in 30m with median > 500ms
- kv-evictions: any eviction rate > 5/min for >5m
- batcher queue > 80% capacity for >5m

mike: tagging some links and notes:
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/serving/rt-overview
- Playbook: /playbooks/serving/rt-latency.md
- Silence template: /runbooks/monitoring/silence-templates.md

deploy-bot: deploy #r1234 rolled at 02:18 UTC to model-serving (reverted by tara at 03:20 UTC)

mike: Thanks team. Will post another quick update if I apply any silences or take actions. Otherwise handing off to alice at 06:00 PT. :rotating_light:

alice: Thanks — appreciate the notes. I'll kick any persistent ones to SRE. :thumbsup:

mike: Handing off now. Good night.
